core.title: Declare every initial Cargo input on the train
core.given: A train definition for which any artifact may be seeded into Cargo before the first wagon step, whether or not a wagon reads it.
core.when: The planner authors or edits the train.
core.then: Declare every artifact Cargo may be seeded with under inputs.caller (caller-provided) or inputs.spec_materialized (deterministically materialized from the spec).
prefer: Classify each initial artifact explicitly: caller-provided goes in inputs.caller; anything derived deterministically from the spec goes in inputs.spec_materialized.
Mark which initial inputs are required so missing ones can be rejected before step 1.
avoid: Relying on an undeclared artifact being present in Cargo at train start; undeclared initial inputs are rejected before step 1.
Leaving a required initial input unsupplied or unmaterialized; missing required initial inputs are rejected before step 1.
Placing non-deterministic or caller-supplied data under inputs.spec_materialized.
core.why: Cargo is seeded and validated before the first wagon step, so the journey can only start from declared initial inputs; undeclared inputs or missing required initial inputs must fail fast before step 1 rather than mid-sequence.
evidence: The train definition contains inputs.caller and/or inputs.spec_materialized listing every artifact seeded into Cargo.
Every artifact that may be seeded into Cargo before step 1 appears in inputs.caller or inputs.spec_materialized.
Running the train with an undeclared initial input or a missing required initial input is rejected before step 1.
verification: Declared initial inputs are the train's inputs.caller and inputs.spec_materialized blocks; these are seeded into Cargo and validated before the first wagon step.

Reject before step 1 when Cargo is seeded with an artifact not declared in inputs.caller or inputs.spec_materialized, or when a required declared initial input is missing; absent optional inputs are not grounds for rejection.
Until an automated validator is bound to this rule, compliance is established by review of the train definition.

values: set of artifacts seeded into Cargo before step 1 changed

fires: Planner authors a new train for which any artifact may be seeded into Cargo (caller-provided or materialized from the spec), including seeded artifacts that no wagon reads.
Planner edits a train so that the set of artifacts that may be seeded into Cargo before step 1 changes.
Planner adds or removes entries under the train's inputs.caller or inputs.spec_materialized.
doesNotFire: Planner edits a wagon's internal acceptances without changing which artifacts may be seeded into Cargo.
Documentation or planning work that does not touch a train definition.
Artifacts produced by an earlier wagon step within the train (those are not initial inputs).

neutralityNotes: The convention is planner-model-level rather than stack-level: train, wagon step, journey, Cargo (the working store seeded before the first wagon step) and the train schema blocks inputs.caller / inputs.spec_materialized are cross-stack ATDD planner vocabulary (train/wagon/journey are artifacts in the closed urn group, and notProfileKeys permits task terms in neutral core activation), so the core keeps them verbatim for fidelity rather than routing them through the profile. The only stack datum needed is the concrete plan-artifact kind of a train definition (roles.plan_artifact.kinds); bun.json names no path, suffix, runner or tooling for train definitions, so no other profile key is required and none is proposed. The activation facts' explanatory notes (train-definition file, diff-level observer) are realization guidance captured by the facts' values and observability. The D2 (#1086) validator binding is the sole realization-only content (bunOnly); until a validator is bound, the core keeps the neutral review-based compliance path.
